podcast.body: This EP from the New Zealand band Tall Dwarfs features the track "The Brain That Wouldn't Die," which serves as an example of the lo-fi sound gaining traction in the mid-1980s. The music was deliberately crafted to sound sonically inferior to the mainstream rock records of its day, showcasing an intentional embrace of low-fidelity aesthetics. "It's from an EP entitled Slug Bucket Hairy Breath Monster and the track is The Brain That Wouldn't Die."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
